item.description: Killington Resort will open for the season tomorrow the seventeenth. First chair will be at ten a.m. or possibly earlier. This is the resort's third winter under independent ownership.

Vermont Fish and Wildlife is issuing antlerless deer permits for the first time in nearly forty years. Hunters must win these permits in a state lottery, each valid for one deer in one wildlife management unit. The permits also apply during muzzleloader season from November thirtieth through December thirteenth for hunters who don't succeed in rifle season.

New York plans to conserve thirty percent of its lands and waters by twenty thirty but is far behind pace. Last year, the state acquired just over six thousand acres, less than one percent of the annual target. Officials are broadening conservation definitions to include private lands and wetlands to help meet the goal.

Vermont is using trees and boulders to protect a road in Jericho from river erosion. An "engineered logjam" of six hundred trees will slow water and catch sediment along Mill Brook. The nine hundred thousand dollar project is funded mostly by FEMA and aims to last longer than concrete fixes.
